messages.subject: Re: some questions with msstats
messages.body_plain:
Yes, you can. Assuming data.res is the output from groupComparisonTMT(), try the following code:

 libarary(MSstats)
 ## profile plot
  data.res$Tvalue <-data.res$log2FC/data.res$SE
  groupComparisonPlots(data=data.res, type="VolcanoPlot", FCcutoff = 2,
                       logBase.pvalue=2)

  # Comparison Plot
  groupComparisonPlots(data=data.res, type="ComparisonPlot")

Yes, you can use the same function but change the type to Heatmap.

 libarary(MSstats)
 ## Heatmap of adjusted p-values for multiple comparisons
  data.res$Tvalue <-data.res$log2FC/data.res$SE
  groupComparisonPlots(data=data.res, type="Heatmap", FCcutoff = 2,
                       logBase.pvalue=2)

messages.subject: Re: some questions with msstats
messages.body_plain: It seems that heatmap function from MSstats is not applicable to your data. Because heatmaps in MSstats require at least two comparisons but your data has only one comparison (ACO-HA). The heatmaps in MSstats is to illustrate up-/down-regulated proteins for multiple comparisons with all proteins. Each row represents each protein. Each column represents each comparison of interest. So it needs at least two columns (two comparisons).

messages.subject: DIA: Annotation and Normalisation with MSstats
messages.subject_clean: DIA: Annotation and Normalisation with MSstats
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats-team,

Recently I performed a DIA experiment using Skyline and I am currently using MSstats for the further processing. I am encountering some problems with which I would really appreciate some help.

First of all, I have some questions about the annotation-file. The setup of my experiment is somewhat complicated since I have three different biological conditions and, within each group,  of some patients I have biological replicates (multiple measurements over time) and for some patients I performed injection replicates as well. I looked at some tutorials on MSstats and if I compare it to this, my setup seems somewhat both a case-control and a time-course experiment. If I try to take both these features into account I get an annotation file such as the one I attached here. However, if I use this, the dataprocessing step somehow seems to get stuck (there is no error but R becomes unresponsive and does not seem to be doing anything). Therefore, for now I just ignored the multiple time points per patient and treated them as individual biological replicates. Since I am not very confident in how MSstats is handeling the data for these different setups I would like to know what the potential harm of this is for my outcome.

Furthermore, I have been struggling a bit with the normalisation options in MSstats. I have tried different options (both equaliseMedian, quantile normalisation and no normalisation) and the outcome of my protein quantification is rather different. I understand that this in itself is not overly surprising, but I am now not feeling very confident in my data. There are mainly two things that worry/surprised me. First of all, there seem to be some samples that are clear outliers (for me so far with unknown cause) in terms of numbers of proteins identified. Some of these samples are injection replicates and in these cases both samples are outliers, indicating to me that this might be sample related (and not so much data processing related). However, what surprises me is that there are some samples that are very low in number of identified proteins when I perform equalise medians, but not if I use quantile normalisation or no normalisation (for example, 4000 proteins vs 600). Again, since I am not very confident in what is happening during these steps in R, it is hard for me to rationalise what causes this difference. Since this is a proteome analysis of a full cell lysate I do not expect to see extremely large differences between samples in terms of the type of proteins I identify. Could you give me an idea where these differences may derive from? Furthermore, if I have samples that are somehow compromised, should I throw them out prior to the final dataprocessing steps? (In other words, could they hamper reliable quantification of proteins in other samples?)

In addition to the mentioned above, I also noticed that the correlation between my injection replicates (same sample, run on the mass spec a few days later, a slightly higher amount) is not super high: around 0.72-0.89 R2. Is this what you would expect? (For comparison; the correlation between non-related samples is around 0.31 R2).
If I look at the correlation between different normalisation methods for a sample, the correlation is also relatively poor (see picture attached). Is there an easy explanation for this that I overlooked? And furthermore, what would you recommend in terms of normalisation?

My apologies for the relatively long question. I really hope you can give me some insights.

Thank you very much in advance,
Donna Olivia Debets
